flashcards.q: Write the BS call formula and explain why the expected return mu does not appear.
flashcards.a: C = S*N(d1) - K*e^{-rT}*N(d2), d1=[ln(S/K)+(r+s^2/2)T]/(s*sqrt(T)), d2=d1-s*sqrt(T). mu vanishes because continuous delta-hedging replicates the payoff synthetically - value equals hedge cost, so only volatility matters, not drift. Price = E^Q[e^{-rT} payoff] under risk-neutral measure.

flashcards.q: State put-call parity and compute P given C=10.45, S=105, K=100, r=5%, T=1.
flashcards.a: C - P = S - PV(divs) - K*e^{-rT}. P = 10.45 - 105 + 100*0.9512 = 0.57. Enables conversions/reversals: long stock = long call + short put + bond leg; parity deviations beyond transaction costs are arbitraged instantly in liquid names.

flashcards.q: State the delta-hedged P&L identity and what it means operationally.
flashcards.a: Hedged P&L per dt ~ 0.5*Gamma*S^2*(sigma_realized^2 - sigma_implied^2)*dt: long gamma earns when realized vol exceeds entry implied; theta is gamma's rent. Implied vol is literally the breakeven realized vol priced into the hedge. It's accounting, not alpha - edge needs a vol FORECAST advantage.

flashcards.q: Where do gamma, vega, and theta peak and how do they scale with time to expiry?
flashcards.a: Gamma peaks ATM near expiry (~1/(sigma*sqrt(T)) scaling - explosive at 0DTE). Vega peaks ATM but GROWS with sqrt(T): a 2y ATM has ~14x vega of a 1-week ATM. Theta most negative ATM short-dated - mirror of gamma. Long options = long gamma + long vega + short theta always.

flashcards.q: What are vanna and volga and who cares about them?
flashcards.a: Vanna = dvega/dS (or ddelta/dvol); volga/vomma = dvega/dvol. They drive wing behavior - why vol desks bucket vegas by strike/tenor instead of netting one number, and why surface shifts (not just parallel vol moves) reprice barrier/tail books materially.

flashcards.q: When exercise American calls early? American puts? What flips at negative rates?
flashcards.a: American CALL on non-dividend stock: never optimal (sell instead). With dividends: just before ex-div when div > remaining time value. American PUT: deep ITM early exercise optimal (interest on K now beats remaining insurance). Negative rates invert carry logic -> earlier put exercise; post-2015 EUR/CHF forced libraries to adapt.

flashcards.q: Why does equity index implied vol skew downward and since when?
flashcards.a: Post-October-1987: permanent OTM put richness from crash-insurance demand plus the leverage effect (equity falls -> debt/equity rises -> vol rises). Constant-sigma BS cannot price gap risk; single names skew steeper than indexes; FX quotes symmetric smiles via 25-delta risk reversals/butterflies.

flashcards.q: Pick models for (a) vanilla book, (b) forward-variance product, and say why each fails outside its lane.
flashcards.a: (a) Vanillas: local vol or SVI-fitted surface - marking to liquid market, dynamics barely matter. (b) Forward variance/VIX options: Heston-class stochastic vol mandatory - local vol locks forward vols to today's surface while empirical forward vol moves independently. Jumps earn their slot for short-dated crash binaries. One big joint model = unfalsifiable black box.

flashcards.q: Set up the canonical control variate for European calls and its math.
flashcards.a: Pair Y=discounted payoff with X=e^{-rT}S_T whose expectation is exactly S0 under Q. Y_cv = Y - beta*(X-E[X]) with beta* = Cov(Y,X)/Var(X); variance shrinks by factor 1/(1-rho^2) - ATM calls rho~0.95+ gives up to ~10x SE cuts. Lab demo: 2.6x SE reduction, error 0.0050->0.0024.

flashcards.q: Name three ways to get Greeks from Monte Carlo and which breaks on digitals.
flashcards.a: Bump-and-revalue (intuitive; noisy for second order, bump-size dilemma), pathwise derivatives (exact for smooth payoffs - FAILS on discontinuous payoffs like digitals/barriers without sigmoid-style smoothing), likelihood-ratio (differentiate density - handles kinks, high variance). AAD computes all Greeks in one backward pass at ~O(1)x pricing cost - standard in bank libraries.

flashcards.q: Rebonato calls IV 'the wrong number to plug into the wrong formula.' So what IS it?
flashcards.a: A standardized QUOTATION unit: the sigma that maps market price through BS. Not a realized-vol forecast, not physical parameter - supply/demand record of insurance preferences across strikes/tenors. Value: comparability, coherent Greeks language, cross-market communication. The formula died as physics but survives as lingua franca.

flashcards.q: How is the VIX calculated and what claim does it approximate?
flashcards.a: Model-free strip of OTM SPX calls+puts integrates to expected 30-day swap variance (2003 methodology): VIX ~ sqrt(E^Q[realized variance]) annualized - approximately the fair strike of a 30-day variance swap. VIX futures trade the variance risk premium: contango most months (~5-10%/mo roll bleed marked ~), violent backwardation in crises (Feb-2018 Volmageddon).

flashcards.q: Design the MC for an arithmetic-average Asian with tight error budget.
flashcards.a: Simulate risk-neutral GBM daily with Brownian-bridge exact averages between steps (kills discretization bias for the averaging feature); control-variate against the GEOMETRIC-average Asian which has a closed form - textbook-perfect CV. Pathwise Greeks valid (smooth payoff). Label all three errors separately: statistical (SE), discretization, model choice.

flashcards.q: What error categories must an MC pricing deliverable label, and why?
flashcards.a: Statistical error (standard error / path count), discretization bias (scheme vs exactness study), model error (process choice - LV vs Heston disagreement reported as range). Convergence precision on a misspecified process is precise nonsense; separating the three keeps model risk auditable (SR 11-7/T24-mrm) instead of laundered inside one SE number.
